1# Paper–code discrepancy register
2
3This register tracks manuscript typos, implementation differences, and unresolved
4questions. The paper is the mathematical reference; a code difference is not
5by itself evidence that the paper is wrong. Preserve entries when resolved,
6recording the resolution and the manuscript version in which it appears.
7
8Source version: `APS_Coincidence_Algebra-14.pdf`.
9Started: 2026-09-08. The manuscript PDF has not been edited.
10
11## Review process
12
13After the first build is agreed ready for validation, audit definitions,
14equations, conventions, and examples against the code and tests. Record the
15code commit and manuscript version used for that audit. Until then this is an
16incremental register, not a claim of complete paper–code agreement.
17
18For each finding, keep a stable ID, paper location/version, printed statement,
19code behavior, evidence, status, and resolution. Distinguish confirmed typos,
20suspected typos, deliberate extensions, and unresolved discrepancies. Link
21regression tests where available. Do not silently resolve differences by
22changing either the paper or the implementation.

24## PA-001 — Detector-count exponent
25
26- **Location:** version 14, Eq. (31), used by Eq. (32).
27- **Status:** Confirmed typo; corrected convention agreed with the author on
28  2026-09-08. Manuscript update pending.
29- **Printed:** denominator N^(k+1) in the power expansion.
30- **Agreed:** for k observed gammas, use N^(k-1). The positive-power factor in
31  Eq. (32) is H = h + h^2/N + h^3/N^2 + ... . If the expansion includes an
32  identity, give it coefficient one and remove it before forming H.
33- **Reason:** the first gamma can hit any detector; each additional gamma must
34  reach that same detector. This assumes whole-array efficiencies, identical
35  detectors, and isotropic emission.
36- **Code:** `DetectionMaps::SummingInExpansion` in
37  `src/Detection/DetectionMaps.cxx`.
38- **Evidence:** `tests/core/test_summing.C` checks N=1, N=2, N=4, and independent
39  cascade enumeration. The single-gamma term is not divided by N.

41## PA-002 — Lower propagation boundary
42
43- **Location:** version 14, Eq. (32).
44- **Status:** Unresolved paper–code discrepancy; proposed boundary clarification.
45  Not yet classified as an author-confirmed typo.
46- **Printed:** lower factor V_source(O), with O = 1 + o + o^2 + ... .
47- **Code:** V_source(O E), where E is the sum of stationary paths at quiver
48  sinks. Only completed downstream cascades contribute.
49- **Reason for current code:** for an upper observed edge followed by a single
50  lower edge, unrestricted projection produces 1 + o_lower, whereas requiring
51  the lower gamma to avoid the detector gives o_lower. The unrestricted sum
52  counts both partial and completed suffixes.
53- **Code:** `DecayProbability::SummingFeedingVector` in
54  `src/Probability/DecayProbability.cxx`.
55- **Evidence:** lower-edge summing-out and multiple-terminal cascade enumeration
56  in `tests/core/test_summing.C`.
57- **Review needed:** verify the manuscript projector/expansion definitions and
58  intended termination convention. Agree the treatment of terminal/metastable
59  levels and observation windows before resolving this entry.

75## PA-003 — Explicit internal-conversion response
76
77- **Location:** version 14, detection maps in Section II.B, Eqs. (28)-(30).
78- **Status:** Implementation convention to reconcile during the audit; not a
79  claimed manuscript typo.
80- **Code convention:** physical edges contain gamma-plus-conversion branching.
81  Efficiencies are conditional on gamma emission. With q = 1/(1+alpha), the
82  hit factor is q * peak_efficiency and the avoidance factor is
83  1 - q * total_efficiency/N.
84- **Review needed:** state whether the paper absorbs the gamma-emission
85  fraction into its efficiencies or requires q explicitly, preventing an
86  omitted or duplicated conversion correction.
87- **Code and evidence:** `DetectionMaps` and `tests/core/test_summing.C`;
88  see `docs/mathematics/internal-conversion.md` and
89  `docs/mathematics/detection-summing.md`.

91## CA-002 — Two-detector gated avoidance and group labels
92
93- **Location:** version 14, Eqs. (71)-(72), pages 10-11.
94- **Status:** Concrete counterexample for the interpretation “two distinct clean
95  full-energy peaks”; observable/general formula needs author review.
96- **Printed:** products use the one-detector summing-out fiber, with gated hit
97  factor h*(N-1)/N. This correctly chooses a different detector for a second
98  single photon, but the o fiber protects only one detector from other photons.
99- **Counterexample:** a deterministic three-photon cascade, perfect peak/total
100  efficiencies, no IC. Select the first two individual photons as clean peaks.
101  The third must avoid both detectors. Enumerating assignments gives
102  (N-1)(N-2)/N^2, whereas the degree-two term of the printed expression gives
103  (N-1)^2/N^2. For N=2 these are 0 and 1/4; for N=4, 3/8 and 9/16.
104- **Implementation:** `AvoidDetectors(tau,2)` supplies 1-2*q*total/N on hidden
105  edges; a restricted resolved-pair calculation is demonstrated in
106  `examples/calculations/coincidence.C`. General summed-in gated groups are not
107  implemented. Their detector partition must be retained rather than inferred
108  from a tensor that has already combined distinct detection scenarios.
109- **Evidence:** `tests/core/test_coincidence_detection.C` checks physical and
110  response-weighted cascade subsets and explicitly enumerates detector
111  assignments for this counterexample. No manuscript edits made.

113## CA-003 — Missing initial population in Table III
114
115- **Location:** version 14, page 10, single-hit row epsilon_2 tensor p_10,
116  column f_2.
117- **Status:** Suspected table typo, not author-confirmed.
118- **Printed:** o_21*h_10, without f_2.
119- **Eq. (70) and code:** f_2*o_21*h_10. All contributions are linear in the
120  initial population; the row must vanish if f_2=0.
121- **Evidence:** mixed-population enumeration in
122  `tests/core/test_coincidence_detection.C`.
